newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market remains still - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market remains still - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Tuesday continued at a standstill, with no sales confirmed, according to feedlot sources.
Packers bid $71.00 per cwt, but were unable to nudge cattle feeders to lower asking levels from $73.00 or $74.00. Top prices last week were $73.00.

Cattle owners were standing firm on asking prices, knowing that showlists were tight again this week, and would probably remain tight for the next two weeks, said Dave Maher of Securities Corp. of Iowa.
Maher added that he expected cattle sales to take place late Tuesday or Wednesday.
About the only cattle moving so far this week were those already earmarked through formulas or contracts.

About 14,000 head were sold the week to date as of mid-afternoon Tuesday in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, including 13,000 formulated and 1,000 previously contracted cattle to be shipped this week, USDA said.
Kansas sales confirmed for the week to date on 4,900 cattle, mostly contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.
